key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D + machine learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cells and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures without exhaustive brute-force simulation.
engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable design rules for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to improve charge extraction, reduce recombination, and accelerate device optimization.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored structures.
Used Leave-One-Group-Out validation and SHAP to rank designs and identify key descriptors.
evidence_signal: The model showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation in cross-validation, and the top predicted devices were confirmed by full SCAPS-1D simulations, including 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: The ML guidance depends on the simulated design space and validation set, so real-device performance may differ due to fabrication variability and unmodeled degradation mechanisms.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
